original_question: Let phi be a plurisubharmonic function on the unit ball B in C^n with well-defined complex Monge-Ampere measure. If (dd^c phi)^n has a Dirac mass at the origin, determine whether phi must have positive Lelong number at 0.
target_in_paper: Section 1.2, Question 7 (Guedj, Rashkovskii): if a plurisubharmonic function phi on the unit ball has a well-defined complex Monge-Ampere measure (dd^c phi)^n and this measure has a Dirac mass at 0, must phi have positive Lelong number at 0?
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the correct ambient space (the unit ball in C^n), the correct class of functions (plurisubharmonic), the key hypothesis that the complex Monge-Ampere measure is well defined, the exact atomic assumption at the origin, and the exact conclusion asked in the paper: positivity of the Lelong number at 0.
missing_details: The paper poses this as an open yes/no problem (Question 7), so the faithful phrasing is 'Is it true that ... ?' rather than 'determine whether ...'.

To be fully stand-alone, specify what 'well-defined complex Monge-Ampere measure' means in the paper: the local Bedford-Taylor notion from Definition 1.1, namely uniqueness of the weak limit of (dd^c phi_j)^n for every decreasing smooth psh approximation on relatively compact subdomains.

Clarify that 'has a Dirac mass at the origin' means the measure has a positive atom at 0, i.e. (dd^c phi)^n({0}) > 0; the paper does not require the whole measure to be supported at 0 in the official formulation.
State the Lelong number explicitly as nu(phi,0).
If one wants the notation completely explicit, the paper uses the standard convention for dd^c fixed in the introduction via omega = dd^c||z||^2.

The paper notes that a concrete sufficient hypothesis ensuring the Monge-Ampere measure is well defined is that phi is locally bounded on B minus {0}, but this is only an example, not part of the official statement.
refined_question: Let B = {z in C^n : ||z|| < 1} be the unit ball, and let phi be a plurisubharmonic function on B such that its complex Monge-Ampere measure (dd^c phi)^n is well defined in the local Bedford-Taylor sense; for example, it is enough to assume that phi is locally bounded on B minus {0}. If (dd^c phi)^n has a Dirac mass at the origin, equivalently if (dd^c phi)^n({0}) > 0, is the Lelong number nu(phi,0) necessarily strictly positive?
justification: The draft is essentially an almost verbatim restatement of the paper's Section 1.2, Question 7. The only paper-specific content it leaves implicit is the precise local meaning of 'well-defined complex Monge-Ampere measure' from Definition 1.1, the fact that local boundedness away from 0 is only a sufficient example and not the official hypothesis, and the precise measure-theoretic reading of 'has a Dirac mass at the origin' as the presence of a positive atom at 0. I therefore keep the target as Question 7 itself, not Demailly's stronger Question 8, which the paper presents only as a stronger route whose positive solution would imply Question 7. I also do not replace Question 7 by the Section 1.3 reduction to the case where the Monge-Ampere measure is concentrated at 0, because that is auxiliary context rather than the official formulation.
